title: Curriculum Vitae
text:
Profile
Biostatistics leader pairing hands-on industry development and FDA regulatory experience across the drug-development lifecycle with a strong academic and methodological foundation. Currently Senior Manager, Biostatistics at Pfizer (Associate Director–equivalent) and a member of the Data Science & Analytics India leadership team, leading a team of statisticians across global Oncology and Inflammation & Immunology programs. Former FDA Oncology Center of Excellence primary reviewer with hands-on NDA/BLA experience, product-labelling negotiation, and pioneering use of real-world evidence and external-control cohorts.

title: SingleBell
text:
SingleBell is a slate, written on in chalk. It gives you one practice for the day, counts it with you, and gets out of the way.
Native SwiftUI. No dependencies. No network code. No account.
Coming to the App Store

title: SingleBell
text:
What it does
The day’s practice. One card each morning, dealt from the week’s shape and what you have already done — clean and press, one-arm swings, snatches — with its warm-up, complex and finisher chalked on the board and an honest estimate of what it costs. Choose short or standard. The day is dealt once and holds until midnight; finishing it resolves the card in place rather than moving it under your feet.
The classics, done properly. Simple & Sinister, Quick and the Dead, Rite of Passage, Armor Building, the Kettlebell Axe, the Humane Burpee and more — each one credited to where it came from, each one adjustable on the slate before you start.
A builder. Make your own: complexes on the clock, the same complexes on a whiteboard where you count the sets, or plain intervals. Keep what you make in Library.
A reference. Every move has a sheet — how it’s done, what it’s for, the cues that matter. The get-up is never dealt to you automatically, because it is a skill before it is a set.
On the Lock Screen. A running practice shows its round and its clock without unlocking the phone. A home-screen widget carries the week’s tally.

title: SingleBell
text:
What it deliberately doesn’t do
No streaks. No badges. No confetti. No charts or stat dashboards. No social feed, no followers, no sharing. No account. No ads. No motivational copy, and not one exclamation mark anywhere in the app.
The absence is the point. A practice you keep is not one you were nagged into.

title: SingleBell
text:
Privacy
Effective 28 August 2026.
SingleBell collects nothing. Not anonymised, not aggregated, not “to improve the experience”. Nothing. The rest of this section is only the detail behind that sentence.

Nothing leaves your phone
The app contains no networking code at all. It does not connect to a server, because there is no server. There is no account to create, nothing to sign in to, and no way for me — or anyone else — to see that you use the app, let alone what you do in it.
There are no analytics, no crash reporters, no advertising identifiers, no attribution frameworks, and no third-party SDKs of any kind.


It asks you for nothing
SingleBell requests no permissions. Not your location, contacts, photos, calendar, microphone, camera, or Health data. It is not integrated with HealthKit. You will never see a permission prompt, because the app declares none.
The coach’s voice is your device’s built-in speech synthesis — sound going out, never sound coming in. Nothing is recorded and nothing is listened to. The app keeps audio running in the background for one reason: so the count keeps speaking when your screen locks mid-set.
The Lock Screen Live Activity is drawn on your device and updated by the app itself. It uses no push token and no notification server.


What is stored, and where
Your practice log, the sessions you save to Library, and your preferences are written to your device’s own storage, in a container shared only between SingleBell and its own widgets — that sharing is what lets the home-screen widget show this week’s tally. That container is on your phone and nowhere else.
If your phone backs itself up to iCloud or to a computer, that backup will include SingleBell’s data exactly as it includes every other app’s. Those backups are covered by Apple’s privacy policy, not by this one.


Deleting it
Delete the app and everything goes with it. There is no copy held anywhere else and nothing to request from me, because I never had it in the first place.


Children
No data is collected from anyone, of any age.


Changes
If any of this ever stops being true, this page will say so before the version that changes it ships, and the date above will change.


Contact
Questions about this policy, or about the app: absk.bhtt@gmail.com. The same address is where to send a bug or a request.

title: Abhishek Bhattacharjee, PhD
text:
I’m Associate Director, Biostatistics at Pfizer in Chennai, on the Data Science & Analytics India leadership team, where I lead a team of statisticians across global Inflammation & Immunology development programs.
My current work sits in I&I, but oncology is where I built my regulatory foundation. Before Pfizer I was a primary statistical reviewer at the FDA’s Oncology Center of Excellence, assessing NDA and BLA submissions across gastric and gastroesophageal cancers, cholangiocarcinoma and other solid tumors, and leading sponsor–agency interactions and labelling negotiations. At Pfizer I served as trial statistician on targeted-therapy programs in non-small cell lung cancer and melanoma.
What holds my attention now are the methods that change what a development program can learn — real-world evidence and target trial emulation, external control cohorts, endpoint consolidation, real-time trial monitoring. I worked on one of the FDA’s early evaluations of non-traditional evidence through the review of a pediatric neuroblastoma program, and I’m building that capability at Pfizer now.
Earlier: a PhD in Statistics from the University of Florida, and two years teaching as a tenure-track assistant professor.
Away from work I build things for iOS. SingleBell is a kettlebell practice app: one bell, the day’s practice dealt each morning, and nothing that collects anything about you.
Views on this site are my own and do not represent my employer.
